requirement_text.REQ-064: Execute Decision 0006's D2 (docs/migration/decisions/0006-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md): drop the tenant_id column from every table whose isolation boundary is the Postgres schema itself, and remove the write-path machinery that populates it. MUST run after REQ-063 -- users and groups are only eligible for the drop once they are per-schema tables (REQ-063 merged as PR #177/5941472, this precondition is satisfied). READ FIRST: decision 0006 in full (sections R1-R3 for why the column goes, section 5 for the consumer inventory, section 6 for exactly what of decision 0003 this supersedes and what it deliberately leaves standing). Decision 0003's Dimension B and its Addendum are the records being partially superseded -- read both so the moduledoc/migration comments this requirement writes describe the new state accurately rather than contradicting a record that still stands in part. TABLES LOSING THE COLUMN (ten): events, events_archive, instance_projections, process_definitions, tokens, tasks, promotion_reviews, promotion_assertion_runs (all already schema-isolated), plus users and groups (schema-isolated by REQ-063). TABLES THAT KEEP IT -- DO NOT TOUCH (decision 0006 D3): tenant_schemas, solution_pack_installs, solution_pack_artefact_bases, pack_update_resolutions. On these four, tenant_id is a real references(:tenants) foreign key on a structurally-global public-schema table and is the only scoping the row has. Dropping it there would be a data-model break, not a cleanup. tenant_role never had the column. TWO COMPOSITE INDEXES SIMPLIFY, and the second carries a contract: promotion_reviews' unique_index([:tenant_id, :plan_digest]) becomes unique_index([:plan_digest]), and promotion_assertion_runs' unique_index([:tenant_id, :idempotency_key]) becomes unique_index([:idempotency_key]). Both are semantically identical inside a per-tenant schema (a leading tenant_id has at most one distinct value there -- the shipped migration headers for events_archive and process_definitions say so themselves). The assertion-runs one backs an idempotency contract consumed via Repo.insert(on_conflict: :nothing, conflict_target: ...) -- restate that contract in the new migration's header and update every conflict_target that names tenant_id. CODE CONSUMERS (decision 0006 section 5, verified inventory): roughly 13 TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call sites exist purely to stamp the column -- 8 in lib/letflow/definitions.ex, 4 in lib/letflow/event_store.ex, 1 in lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex. Sites that bind {:ok, _tenant_id} and discard it are validating the prefix string's shape, not stamping; decide per-site whether that validation is still wanted (a valid_prefix?/1-style guard) or removable, and say which in the moduledoc. DO NOT DELETE tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 itself -- REQ-063's data copy needs it and decision 0006 D4's future reporting mechanism may. Only its stamping call sites go. Ten schema modules drop field(:tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) and its cast/validate_required entries: Engine.Task, Engine.Token (note: REQ-063 renamed the tokens-table schema module to Engine.TokenRecord, and REQ-044 separately claimed Engine.Token for its own in-memory struct -- confirm which module actually owns the tokens table's tenant_id field before editing, do not assume the requirement text's original naming still matches current lib/ state), EventStore.Event, EventStore.ArchivedEvent, EventStore.InstanceProjection, Definitions.ProcessDefinition, Definitions.PromotionReview, Definitions.PromotionAssertionRun, Identity.User, Identity.Group. Moduledoc blocks in Engine.Task/Engine.TokenRecord ("tenant_id is never caller-supplied") and Identity.User ("intra-schema column per Decision B") document a column that will no longer exist and must be removed with it, not left describing a field that is gone. SCOPE BOUNDARY: does not build decision 0006 D4's cross-tenant reporting mechanism (no consumer exists; a future requirement owns it). Does not revisit Decision B's schema-per-tenant isolation choice, which 0006 section 6 explicitly leaves standing. Does not add a session-GUC tenant context.

task.description:
Produce lib/letflow/design/req064-drop-tenant-id.md covering every module this requirement touches, per WF-02 Step 1's procedure. Design-only: no implementation code, function signatures and @spec-style shapes only.

FIRST, before designing anything: verify current lib/ state against the requirement text's module names, which were written before REQ-063 shipped and before REQ-044's own naming claims. Specifically confirm what Ecto schema module currently owns the tokens table (the requirement text says Engine.Token but flags that REQ-063 may have renamed it to Engine.TokenRecord to avoid REQ-044's own Engine.Token in-memory struct -- read lib/letflow/engine/ directly and state which module actually has the tenant_id field to drop). Do the same sanity check for every other of the ten named modules -- do not trust the requirement text's module names blindly, confirm each against the real file.

Specifically design: (1) one migration (or a small number, ELIXIR-DEV's implementation choice within your design's guidance) that drops tenant_id from the ten confirmed tables, applied per-tenant-schema via the same tenant_scoped_migrations/0 mechanism -- state the exact ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN shape and the prefix()-truthiness guard each carries. (2) the two composite-index simplifications (promotion_reviews, promotion_assertion_runs) -- exact before/after index definitions, and the promotion_assertion_runs idempotency contract restated explicitly for the migration header. (3) for each of the ~13 tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call sites in definitions.ex/event_store.ex/promotion_review_store.ex: state per-site whether it's removed entirely (was stamping the now-gone column) or kept as a lighter-weight validation (was only checking {:ok, _} and discarding) -- do not blanket-decide, the requirement text explicitly asks for a per-site call. (4) the exact field/cast/validate_required removal for each of the ten schema modules, using the CORRECTED module list from your own verification step, not the requirement text's possibly-stale one. (5) the exact moduledoc text changes for Engine.Task/TokenRecord and Identity.User that currently describe a soon-to-not-exist column.

Read decision 0006 in full (sections R1-R3, 5, 6) and decision 0003 (Dimension B + Addendum) before designing -- section 6 states precisely what's superseded and what stands; your design's moduledoc-text guidance must be consistent with both, not contradict either.

result.summary: Produced lib/letflow/design/req064-drop-tenant-id.md. Corrected the tokens-table module ownership: Letflow.Engine.TokenRecord owns tokens.tenant_id (not Engine.Token, which is REQ-044's unrelated pure in-memory struct with zero Ecto dependency) -- verified by direct read of both lib/letflow/engine/token.ex and token_record.ex. All other nine named modules matched the requirement text exactly on direct re-check. Design covers: (1) ten migrations dropping tenant_id, each with the mandatory if prefix() do guard and remove(:tenant_id, :binary_id) for reversibility, registered via tenant_scoped_migrations/0's three-element manifest form; (2) both composite-index simplifications (promotion_reviews, promotion_assertion_runs) with exact before/after index/constraint definitions and the idempotency contract restated for the migration header, plus a third tenant_id-leading index found on `users` during this session's direct read (not named in the requirement text) that also needs dropping, flagged as an open question on replacement; (3) all 14 tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call sites (corrected count from the requirement text's ~13 -- definitions.ex actually has 9 sites, not 8), each given an explicit per-site removed/kept-as-validation/kept-unchanged decision, including two sites (activate/2, rollback_definition_version/4) that use tenant_id for a genuine functional purpose unrelated to the dropped column and must NOT be touched; (4) field/cast/validate_required removal for all ten corrected schema modules, including two unique_constraint/2 calls that must drop their leading :tenant_id to keep matching their simplified index names; (5) exact moduledoc replacement text for TokenRecord, Task, User, Group, and all three EventStore modules (a fourth+fifth moduledoc site beyond the two the requirement text named, found by direct read), plus confirmation that ProcessDefinition/PromotionReview/PromotionAssertionRun have no dedicated tenant_id prose to edit. Explicitly stated: the four D3 tables are untouched (no file for them may appear in ELIXIR-DEV's diff), and tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 itself is not deleted. Four open questions recorded (§7) rather than silently resolved: the apply_promotion_assertion_rerun/6 tenant_id binding's full call-graph trace, the users third index's replacement-or-not, migration file grouping granularity, and whether to trim event_store.ex's ctx map. No implementation code written -- signatures, exact cast/validate_required/index/constraint shapes, and moduledoc prose only.
